coaching.headline: A clean 27-minute ranked win built on fight volume: 9 fights won to the opponent's 2, 6 of them cashed into a tower or camp inside 90 seconds, and an 8-1 tower sweep to close it out.
coaching.team: Lane phase opened well: Kira held the edge over Revenant the whole game, Renna and Scarlett were both ahead early against Wraith and Shinbi, and only the support lane, Maco against Steel, went the other way. Maco still grabbed first blood on Revenant at 2.4 minutes. Off the lane, the neutral map told a quieter story: the enemy won the river battle 13 contests to 8 and took all three of the game's early river seedlings, including a Mini Prime at minute 13 that went to them with the whole team alive and nobody sent to stop it. The one real fight lost early was the 6.9 loss at our Fangtooth, a 2v2 with mid and offlane both already ahead in their own lanes and free to rotate in. From the 8.2-minute teamfight at our Outer Tower onward, fights started going our way in bulk, nine won for the game against two lost. One more bad trade came at 15.5 in our own jungle, giving up two bodies for nothing with no objective up. Fangtooth, Orb Prime and Primal Fangtooth all fell to us through the mid game, with the 3-0 fight next to our Orb Prime at 23.1 securing that camp and the Primal Fangtooth following about two minutes later. Vision favored us throughout, 34 wards placed to 27, and the only clean individual mistake all game was Renna caught alone by Khaimera at 17.8, against three such deaths on the other side. Towers finished 8-1, and a 4-1 fight at our Inhibitor at 26.4 opened the core seconds later. Next game: contest the river and seedling camps early instead of conceding them the way the Mini Prime went at minute 13. Also rotate a winning lane into a fight in progress the way the 6.9 and 15.5 losses needed.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: Two moments shifted it. The 6.9 loss at our Fangtooth was answered right away by a won teamfight at our Outer Tower at 8.2, and fights that had been close started going our way from there. Then the fight next to our Orb Prime at 23.1, won 3-0, secured that objective, and the Primal Fangtooth followed about two minutes later, putting the game out of reach before the 4-1 fight at our Inhibitor at 26.4 closed it.
coaching.whatWorked: The one throughline was fight volume and conversion: the team won 9 fights to the opponent's 2, and 6 of those wins were cashed into a tower or camp within 90 seconds, while the opponent converted zero of its two. That habit, on top of an 8-1 tower count, is what turned a mostly-even lane phase into a 27-minute rout.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324's Kira was the story of both the lane and the game: 9 kills, 4 deaths, 9 assists, and the match's highest damage to heroes at 43,385. The carry lane against Revenant read favored the entire game, and six of Kira's nine kills came directly off Revenant in a running duel that also cost three of Kira's four deaths to the same hero — the matchup ran hot both ways, but Kira won it. That dueling dominance is a big part of why the carry lane read favored us the entire game.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31's Maco opened the game with first blood on Revenant at 2.4 minutes and closed with the team's highest healing at 23,948, exactly the sustain role this comp needed, on 6 kills, 3 deaths and 11 assists. The support lane against Steel went the other way the whole game, and Maco died in both of the fights the team lost this game, the 6.9 loss at our Fangtooth and the 15.5 bad trade in our own jungle. The build carried no armor into a comp that ran three physical damage sources, a flag the facts raise directly, though Tainted Totem's anti-heal did have a real target in Khaimera's self-sustain.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's Scarlett won the individual exchanges with Shinbi early, three of Scarlett's four kills came off that matchup, the fourth off Khaimera in the 16.2 teamfight, for a clean 4-kill, 2-death game as the team's only listed frontline. The build's lone defensive item, Aegis Of Agawar, wasn't online until roughly minute 25 by the item timeline, leaving Scarlett without armor for most of the game against a comp that ran three physical damage sources. The second death came in the 24.7 fight near our Primal Fangtooth; the team had 4 bodies to their 3 there, but Renna had gone down 32 seconds earlier, so it was never the clean man-advantage fight the raw numbers suggest, and it still only traded 2-2.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs's Renna was the most active finisher in the second half, picking up all 7 of her kills spread across Wraith (three), Khaimera (two) and Revenant (two) as the fights swung our way. The build matched the hero's winning metaCore exactly, Entropy, Wraith Leggings and Overseer, before adding Oblivion Crown as a pure-damage fourth slot. The one clean coaching note: Renna was caught alone by Khaimera at 17.8 minutes, outside of any grouped fight, the team's single avoidable death of the game.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim's Aurora ran the best KDA on the roster, 7 kills and only 2 deaths across the full 27 minutes, with 20,984 damage to objectives, a mix of survivability and camp pressure that fed the tower and objective lead all game. Aurora's build ran tankier than the hero's meta core, swapping Elafrost and Gaia Greaves for Tainted Guard's anti-heal bleed, a direct counter to a Khaimera whose whole kit runs on the health regen his passive grants. Three of Aurora's seven kills came on Wraith, mostly cleaning up fights the team had already grouped for.

6.9.call: Kira and Maco fought Revenant and Steel 2v2 at our Fangtooth and lost it 0-2. Both the midlane and offlane were already ahead in their own lanes and free to rotate in, and sending one of them there instead flips the numbers before the fight even starts.

8.2.call: The response to that loss was immediate: a 4-man fight won 3-1 at our Outer Tower, with the tower falling inside the next minute. That is the right sequence: win the group fight, then spend it on the structure sitting next to it.

15.5.call: No objective was up when Kira and Maco fought Steel and Revenant 2v2 deep in our own jungle, and it went 0-2. Xeebs was ahead in the midlane and could have rotated to even the numbers, while the offlane was pinned and losing and wasn't a realistic source of help; without a prize on the line, resetting was the better call than fighting.

18.8.call: A clean 4-for-0 next to our Fangtooth doubled as the camp secure, the shape of fight this comp wants: group up and win it on top of the objective.

21.5.call: Won 2-0 at our Inner Tower with an item-count edge, but it didn't convert into a tower or camp within the tracking window, one of three won fights this game left uncashed. Walking a won fight straight into the closest objective is the fix each time.

23.1.call: 3-0 next to our Orb Prime took that camp, with the Primal Fangtooth following about two minutes later, one of the biggest swings of the mid-game.

26.4.call: The closing fight: 4-1 at our own Inhibitor with towers already 8-1, and the core fell seconds later. With that much of a structural lead already built, the call was simply to keep grouping and let it close.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Kira's completed build was Tainted Rounds, Ruination and Imperator instead of the community's Solaris-Ashbringer-Imperator core. Tainted Rounds' 45% healing cut and Ruination's mana-drain bleed are answers to enemy sustain, but the enemy fielded no healers at all this game, so that half of the build had nothing to cut. The core it skipped adds an empowered on-hit crit-capable proc (Solaris) and an 8% cooldown reduction on every successful basic attack (Ashbringer) — exactly the cooldown reset Kira's kit needs to reposition with Shadow Glide and keep landing the channeled Purge. Six of Kira's nine kills came off Revenant in a running duel that also cost three deaths to the same hero, and more cooldown uptime is the kind of thing that swings duels like that.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: The engine's pick for Kira is Demiurge, which adds 12% more stats from every item and 10% more damage from item effects, a scaling major that rewards reaching a finished build rather than any single early spike, matching a kit whose own win condition is stacking Vengeance into a late Purge. The trade is no durability or sustain of its own, so it leans on a frontline soaking damage in front of her, which held up with Scarlett anchoring the front line this game. This is theoretical: the match feed does not record which Eternal was actually equipped.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Maco's four items, Crescelia, Windcaller, Everbloom and Tainted Totem, all trigger off Maco's own heals or on-hit procs rather than off the missing metaCore piece, Enra's Blessing, which shields an ally the instant they're locked down. Against an enemy comp the facts flag directly, three physical damage sources and no armor built at all, a proactive shield on lockdown is exactly the tool a pinned support needs, and Maco was on the losing end of both fights the team lost this game. The healing that did get built paid off elsewhere: Maco's 23,948 healing was the team's highest, and Tainted Totem's anti-heal bleed had a real target in Khaimera's self-sustain.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: The engine's pick for Maco is Vesh, whose major turns ability hits into a damage-over-time effect that scales with game length, a fit for an ability-based kit like Maco Gift! and the charged Strike ultimate rather than an auto-attack build. It trades away any proactive peel tool for that damage, which lines up with a support who spent the game on the wrong end of the lane against Steel and lost both fights that went badly. This is theoretical: the match feed does not record which Eternal was actually equipped.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Scarlett's four items, Syonic Echo, Overlord, Aegis Of Agawar and Terminus, are all off the tracked meta core for the hero and role, so there is no completed-core comparison to draw from directly. The one item that carries any armor, Aegis Of Agawar's 10% (20% at low health) physical and magical armor, wasn't online until roughly minute 25 by the item timeline, which lines up with the matchup flag on record: no armor built against a comp running three physical damage sources for most of the game. Scarlett still finished 4 kills and 2 deaths as the team's only listed frontline, winning the early lane against Shinbi before it settled even.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: The engine's pick for Scarlett is Krix, a health-stacking major that adds a growing percentage of max health plus bonus hitbox size, a fit for the team's lone frontline holding the line against three physical damage dealers. The trade is a burst or damage-scaling major instead, which two of the team's own damage carries, Kira and Renna, already cover, so durability over burst is the reasonable read for this comp. This is theoretical: the match feed does not record which Eternal was actually equipped.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Renna's build matched the hero's winning metaCore exactly, Entropy, Wraith Leggings and Overseer, all three items in the sample that wins 57.5% of games with this build. Entropy adds bonus damage on every ability hit, Wraith Leggings adds a flat 12% to all ability damage, and Overseer boosts and heals off the ultimate specifically, a full ability-damage stack that a fourth slot, off-meta Oblivion Crown's flat magic power, only added more of rather than any survivability. That lines up with Renna's own kit read as fragile and reliant on her zones: five deaths across the game, including one caught alone by Khaimera outside of any grouped fight at 17.8 minutes.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: The engine's pick for Renna is Demiurge, the same item-scaling major as Kira's, adding 12% more stats from items and 10% more damage from item effects, a natural fit for a build that is already three item-triggered procs deep. The trade is the same lack of survivability the build itself leans into, consistent with getting caught alone once and dying five times overall even in a game the team won comfortably. This is theoretical: the match feed does not record which Eternal was actually equipped.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Aurora's actual build, Magnify, Orb Of Enlightenment, Tainted Guard and Flux Matrix, swapped out the metaCore's Elafrost and Gaia Greaves, which would have added the same class of physical armor plus a cast-slow and a movement-stacking burst proc, for Tainted Guard's 55 physical armor with a built-in 45% healing-reduction bleed and Flux Matrix's 45 magical armor. Against a Khaimera whose whole kit runs on the health regen from his own passive, that anti-heal is a direct answer the meta core doesn't carry, and the tankier mix of both armor types paid off: only 2 deaths across 27 minutes while still putting up 20,984 damage to objectives.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: The engine's top pick for Aurora is Demiurge, an item-scaling major, though her build ran a tankier line than that call assumes. Her second-best modeled option, Krix, adds a growing percentage of max health instead, which fits a control-tank kit whose win condition is landing a full crowd-control chain and surviving to do it again. Either way the trade is the same, less raw item-effect damage for more time on the field to land that chain, and Aurora's 2 deaths this game support the durability-first read. This is theoretical: the match feed does not record which Eternal was actually equipped.

synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Maco) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Mercy poke → stack Vengeance → Shadow Glide reposition → Purge ult
ourKits.winCondition: stack Vengeance and shred with the channeled Purge
ourKits.playWith: peel so she can channel Purge safely
ourKits.playAgainst: interrupt/CC her during Purge; punish her short dash cooldown

ourKits.combo: Maco Gift! (heal ally / hurt enemy) → Maco Fly! slam → Maco Strike! charged line ult
ourKits.winCondition: poke and heal-flex while landing the charged ult
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge the charged Strike; pressure his low survivability

ourKits.combo: Soulfire waves → Mortal Coil pull-zone → Stupor orb → Abyssal Rift zone
ourKits.winCondition: zone a fight with Mortal Coil + ult and chunk from range
ourKits.passive: consumes essences from kills for power
ourKits.playWith: frontline to hold enemies in her zones
ourKits.playAgainst: fragile and reliant on her zones — flank/dive around the telegraphs

ourKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
ourKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
ourKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
ourKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

enemyKits.combo: Peekaboo! mark+slow → Knock, Knock! sniper → Back It Up! displacement ult
enemyKits.winCondition: land long-range snipes on marked targets and reset on takedowns
enemyKits.playWith: engage that holds a target in his sniper line
enemyKits.playAgainst: close the gap — he's weak point-blank; dodge the skillshot snipe

enemyKits.combo: Ambush leap → Unleash AS → Cull stun, Invigorate to cleanse+heal
enemyKits.winCondition: stick on one target, stun with Cull and out-sustain via Spirit Regen
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his Cull stun
enemyKits.playAgainst: ANTI-HEAL is mandatory — it guts his whole kit; kite the leap and CC through Invigorate

enemyKits.combo: Rushing Beat dashes → Line Tempo wolves → Circle Rhythm shield → All-Kill! wolfpack ult
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Track and unleash All-Kill! in a grouped fight
enemyKits.playAgainst: spread vs the wolfpack; she's squishy without her shield up

enemyKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
enemyKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
enemyKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
enemyKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Scar mark → Obliterate homing missiles → Reckoning 1v1 realm ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Reckoning a target into the Nether Realm and crit them down 1v1
enemyKits.playWith: a team to clean up if his 1v1 stalls
enemyKits.playAgainst: the ult is a 1v1 — peel the realmed ally can't help, so don't be caught alone; he's crit-reliant early-weak
